summary: The Green Bay Packers beat the Kansas City Chiefs 27-19 in Week 13 'Sunday Night Football' at Lambeau Field, led by Jordan Love's three-touchdown, no-interception performance. The game ended amid controversy over uncalled or questionable penalties on the final drive, including a dubious unnecessary roughness call on Jonathan Owens and a missed pass interference. The note is a live-blog with quarter-by-quarter updates, final score, Taylor Swift's attendance, and broadcast details.
one_line: Packers edged the Chiefs 27-19 on Sunday Night Football behind Jordan Love's three touchdowns, in a game marred by controversial final-drive officiating.
key_facts: The Packers beat the Chiefs 27-19 in Week 13 'Sunday Night Football' at Lambeau Field on Dec. 3, 2023.
Final score by quarter: Chiefs 3, 3, 6, 7 (19); Packers 7, 7, 7, 6 (27).
Jordan Love completed 25-of-36 passes for 267 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions.
It was Love's fourth game of the year with three touchdowns and no interceptions, tied for most in the league.
Love's first career start came against the Chiefs in 2021.
Ben Sims caught his first career NFL touchdown from Love on the opening drive, making it 7-0 Packers.
Rookie kicker Anders Carlson hit a 40-yard field goal and a 48-yard field goal to put the Packers up 27-19 late.
Packers cornerback Keisean Nixon intercepted Patrick Mahomes' pass at 10:59 p.m. to break up a Chiefs drive.

Referees flagged Jonathan Owens for an unnecessary roughness call on Mahomes that the article calls baffling, giving the Chiefs 20 yards; a later possible pass interference on Carrington Valentine against Marquez Valdes-Scantling went uncalled.
Isiah Pacheco was ejected for throwing a punch at Nixon, after having topped 100 rushing yards and scored a touchdown.
Mahomes' final-play Hail Mary fell incomplete, with contact by Owens on Travis Kelce going uncalled.
Taylor Swift attended the game with Brittany Mahomes to watch Travis Kelce and the Chiefs.
The game aired on NBC and Peacock with Mike Tirico, Cris Collinsworth and Melissa Stark, with kickoff at 8:20 p.m. ET.
